candidates.exact_span:
1. The permittee shall handle and dispose of sewage sludge in accordance with Section 405 of the
      Clean Water Act and all other applicable Federal regulations to protect public health and the
      environment from any reasonably anticipated adverse effects due to any toxic pollutants which
      may be present.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which Section 405 and other federal pollutant criteria are incorporated, and whether they impose enforceable numeric limits versus general performance standards, could change which limits are deemed applicable for comparison to reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span:
2. If requirements for sludge management practices or pollutant criteria become more stringent than
      the sludge pollutant limits or acceptable management practices in this permit, or control a
      pollutant not listed in this permit, this permit may be modified or revoked and reissued to
      conform to the requirements promulgated at Section 405(d)( 2) of the Clean Water Act.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether more stringent Section 405(d)(2) criteria are treated as superseding in-permit limits, or as merely potential future modifications, affects which numeric pollutant limits are considered enforceable for FY2025 compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span:
3. In all cases, if the person (permit holder) who prepares the sewage sludge or supplies the sewage
      sludge to another person (owner or operator of a sewage sludge unit) for disposal in a surface
      disposal site, the permit holder shall provide all necessary information to the parties who receive
      the sludge to assure compliance with these regulations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of what constitutes 'all necessary information' and who bears documentation duties affects whether missing monitoring or limit-evidence gaps are classified as documented no-data, inadequate evidence, or unresolved.

candidates.exact_span:
4. The permittee shall give prior notice to EPA (Chief, Permits Branch, Water Management
      Division, Mail Code 6WQ -P, EPA Region 6, 1445 Ross Avenue, Dallas, Texas 75202) of any
      planned changes in the sewage sludge disposal practice, in accordance with 40 CFR Part
      122.41(l)(1)(iii). These changes may justify the application of permit conditions that are different
      from or absent in the existing permit. Change in the sludge use or disposal practice may because
      for modification of the permit in accordance with 40 CFR Part 122.62(a)(1).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a disposal-practice change occurred and triggered modified permit conditions determines which numeric limits and monitoring requirements are treated as applicable during FY2025 versus those in the base permit text.

candidates.exact_span:
5. The permittee or owner/operator shall submit a written closure and post closure plan to the
      permitting authority 180 days prior to the closure date. The plan shall include the following
      information:
candidates.computation_change_reason: The timing and occurrence of closure relative to FY2025 determines whether post-closure obligations apply and how missing or partial evidence around closure is classified.

candidates.exact_span:
a. A discussion of how the leachate collection system will be operated and maintained for three
          years after the surface disposal site closes if it has a liner and leachate collection system.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the site 'has a liner and leachate collection system' is a conditional trigger; different readings of that condition change whether leachate-related operational and monitoring obligations were required and how absent leachate evidence is categorized.

candidates.exact_span:
b. A description of the system used to monitor continuously for methane gas in the air in any
          structures within the surface disposal site. The methane gas concentration shall not exceed
          25% of the lower explosive limit for methane gas for three years after the sewage sludge unit
          closes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage couples continuous methane monitoring with an enforceable 25% LEL ceiling over a post-closure window; interpretation of closure date, LEL value, structure scope, and FY2025 overlap changes limit applicability, monitoring duty, and missing-data classification.

candidates.exact_span:
closes. A description of the system used to monitor for methane gas in the air at the property
          line of the site shall be included. The methane gas concentration at the surface disposal site
          property line shall not exceed the lower explosive limit for methane gas for three years after
          the sewage sludge unit closes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage sets property-line methane monitoring and a distinct 100% LEL limit over a post-closure window; different readings of closure timing, site boundary, and monitoring frequency affect limit comparisons, obligation applicability, and missing-evidence semantics.

candidates.exact_span:
c. A discussion of how public access to the surface disposal site will be restricted for three
          years after it closes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether access-restriction measures constitute a monitoring or reporting obligation, and whether closure occurred within the relevant FY2025 window, affects obligation applicability and how absent documentation is interpreted.

candidates.exact_span:
1. An active sewage sludge unit located within 60 meters of a fault that has displacement in
      Holocene time shall close by March 22, 1994.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'active,' fault proximity, and Holocene displacement determines whether the unit should have been closed before FY2025, which in turn affects which ongoing versus post-closure requirements and evidence expectations apply.

candidates.exact_span: 2. An active sewage sludge unit located in an unstable area shall close by March 22, 1994.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a site qualifies as an 'unstable area' and remained 'active' after the 1994 deadline changes which management and monitoring obligations are treated as applicable during FY2025 and how missing evidence is resolved.

candidates.exact_span: 3. An active sewage sludge unit located in a wetland shall close by March 22, 1994.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of wetland status and whether the unit was still 'active' in or before FY2025 affects which requirements govern the period and whether monitoring gaps reflect conditional non-requirement or unresolved obligation.

candidates.exact_span: 4. Surface disposal shall not restrict the flow of the base 100-year flood.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this non-numeric performance standard is treated as an enforceable limit with a measurable compliance basis, and whether flood-related monitoring or demonstration is required, affects limit-evaluation rows and monitoring-obligation determinations.

candidates.exact_span:
5. The run-off collection system for an active sewage sludge unit shall have the capacity to handle
      run-off from a 25-year, 24-hour storm event.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'capacity,' the 25-year/24-hour design storm, and whether the unit was 'active' during FY2025 affects whether this is an applicable enforceable standard for comparison and whether runoff-related monitoring or demonstration was required.

candidates.exact_span: 6. A food crop, feed crop, or a fiber crop shall not be grown on a surface disposal site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether crop-growth prohibition implies associated monitoring, inspection, or reporting obligations, and how absence of crop-related evidence is classified, depends on interpretation of this requirement's operative scope.
